To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Monospecific anti‐ GD1b IgG was detected in sera of rabbits with experimental sensory ataxia.

(1) IgG antibody monospesific to GD1b, a glycolipid antigen, is required to induce experimental sensory ataxia in rabbits; (2) the IgG antibody monopospecific to GD 1b binds to the large neuronal cytoplasma of rabbit dorsal root gagnlia; and (3) the antibody‐binding to the large neuronal cells may be responsible for the sensory ataxia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of GD1b‐specific IgG on rabbit dorsal root ganglion neurons.
